At the heart of this urban centre is a vast expanse of greenery, including a botanical garden.

stories.title: India's Pant joins New Zealand club match under false name
stories.summary: India wicketkeeper Rishabh Pant made a surprise appearance for a club team in Christchurch under the false name 'Stan Stan'. Pant, 29, played for the Open House Swingers against The Chosen Ones and smashed 54 from 21 balls in a 16-run win. His appearance came a day before India's second Test against New Zealand, which begins at the Hagley Oval at 22:00 GMT on Thursday.

stories.title: 'Who's got the mints?': Nathan Lyon named in alleged ball-tampering plot
stories.summary: A report by CODE Sports has identified the veteran spinner as the player who reportedly asked for the sweets during Australia's Test against Pakistan in the UAE. Earlier this week, veteran journalist Gerard Whateley had revealed that an unnamed Australian player had asked, "Who's got the mints?" According to the report, a substitute fielder was then sent to look through the players' bags for red frogs.

stories.title: How John Wright spotted Jasprit Bumrah
stories.summary: The photograph of John Wright alongside Jasprit Bumrah when the duo met in Lincoln, on the outskirts of Christchurch during India A’s match against New Zealand A, that went viral on social media recently may have offered a reminder of the fast bowler’s extraordinary journey.

stories.title: Hasn’t looked dangerous with second new ball: Sunil Gavaskar highlights Jasprit Bumrah's lack of zip
stories.summary: Former India captain Sunil Gavaskar expressed a word of caution regarding Jasprit Bumrah , saying the pacer didn't look threatening with the second new ball on Day 1 of the second Test at Christchurch on Friday. The 32-year-old's pace was relatively down in the final session at the Hagley Oval, with speeds hovering in the 127-130 kmph range.

stories.title: Donald shines again as England outclass Aussies
stories.summary: England reaffirmed their advantage over a struggling Australia in white-ball cricket with a seven-wicket thrashing in the third T20 at The Gabba. Fresh from their eight-wicket win on Tuesday, England bowled Australia out for 108 - the lowest total the hosts have been dismissed for in a T20 at home.

stories.title: Twickenham set to be half empty for Nations Championship finals opening night
stories.summary: BBC Sport rugby union news reporter Published 9 minutes ago The start of the Nations Championship finals weekend will play out in front of thousands of empty seats on Friday with Twickenham's Allianz Stadium set to be filled to about half its 82,000-seater capacity. The uppermost tier of the stadium is entirely closed, while just over half of the middle tier is open.

stories.title: Eight-time champion Marquez to retire from MotoGP
stories.summary: MotoGP champion Marc Marquez has said he will retire days after clinching a record-equalling eighth title. The 33-year-old Spaniard clinched the 2026 title in Portugal last weekend and will end his professional career after the final race of the season in Valencia. The Ducati rider's latest triumph puts him level with Giacomo Agostini and one clear of modern great Valentino Rossi.

stories.title: EFL preview: Happy Potters and the deathly Hammers
stories.summary: You've dug the de-icer and novelty jumpers out the back of the cupboard and within days a square of chocolate before breakfast will be socially acceptable again. December is looming large, but you can be sure the season of goodwill does not extend to the English Football League.

stories.title: Overton runs riot with 5-wicket haul as Australia register lowest-ever home T20I total
stories.summary: In a disheartening performance, Australia limped to just 108 runs in the third T20I against England at the Gabba. Captain Harry Brook's tactical decision to bowl first was validated as Jamie Overton shone with an impressive five-wicket haul. England's bowlers systematically dismantled Australia's batting order, ultimately leading to the team's second-lowest T20I total against their rivals.

stories.title: 'I want us to go all the way': PV Sindhu eyes historic Uber Cup triumph as India gets 2028 hosting rights
stories.summary: Sindhu was part of the Indian women's squad that created history by securing the country's first-ever Uber Cup medal, a bronze, when New Delhi hosted the tournament in 2014. "I was proud of the bronze we won in Delhi in 2014. If I get another chance to play the Uber Cup at home, I want us to go all the way.

stories.title: Why COP31 was more than a failure of negotiations
stories.summary: The immediate trigger was a “cover text” put forward by COP 31 president Murat Kurum, Turkiye’s Environment Minister. This is an overarching political decision that frames the outcome of a conference and is usually finalised last. Like every outcome, it needs the agreement of all parties. No country or bloc holds a veto but every clause must be accepted by all 190-plus delegations.

stories.title: Mint explainer: why HPV vaccination is critical for girls as India crosses 10 million doses
stories.summary: India has administered more than 10 million doses of the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine to 14-year-old girls in less than nine months under a campaign by the Union health ministry. The drive has covered nearly 87% of the annual target cohort of about 12 million girls, drawing praise from the World Health Organization’s (WHO) South-East Asia Region.

stories.title: Can genomics help us understand cancer better? | Hindustan Times
stories.summary: Cancer diagnosis is entering a new era, moving beyond identifying the presence of a tumour towards understanding its underlying biology. While conventional diagnostic methods remain fundamental to cancer detection and classification, advances in molecular profiling and genomic testing are helping clinicians uncover the genetic alterations that drive tumour growth, influence disease progression and determine potential responses to treatment.

stories.title: Do Indian bodies burn calories differently? Country’s 1st advanced metabolic chamber seeks answers
stories.summary: The Human Metabolic Chamber at Vellore’s Christian Medical College (CMC) was jointly established by the college and the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research’s (TIFR) Advanced Research Unit on Metabolism, Development and Aging (ARUMDA) and is designed to give researchers a more precise picture of how the human body burns calories and uses different sources of energy.

stories.summary: SpaceX has received approval from the US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to deploy up to 1 million orbital computing modules for a proposed constellation of space-based data centres, marking a major push to take artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure beyond Earth.

stories.title: Explainer-Spain’s snap election — why it matters and who might win?
stories.summary: MADRID, Nov 26 (Reuters) – Spain goes to the polls on Sunday in an early parliamentary election that may usher in a right-wing coalition to replace the Socialist-led minority government of Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, one of Europe’s last leftist leaders. Sanchez called the election after parliament on October 2 rejected his decrees to address growing anger over rising rents and evictions.

stories.title: Can 20 rebel TMC MPs vote on delimitation in Parliament? Why Speaker's call matters | HT Explainers
stories.summary: With the government preparing to return to Parliament next week with a Constitution amendment that requires a two-thirds majority, the fate of 20 Trinamool Congress (TMC) MPs facing disqualification proceedings before Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla could have a bearing on the legislative arithmetic.

stories.title: Who Is Vardhaman Jain? Chennai Businessman Offers 121 Kg Gold Ornaments Worth ₹206 Cr To Lord Venkateswara
stories.summary: Chennai-based industrialist and philanthropist Vardhaman Jain has made a significant religious contribution by donating 121 kg of gold ornaments valued at ₹160 crore to the Tirumala Temple in Andhra Pradesh. Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu visited the temple on Thursday, Nov 26, to attend the formal handover ceremony.

stories.title: Why Are SCs, STs, OBCs, Minorities Missing From Collegium Picks? Ex-CJI BR Gavai Flags Representation Gap
stories.summary: Former Chief Justice of India (CJI) BR Gavai has raised questions over alleged bias in recent Supreme Court collegium recommendations for judicial appointments and transfers, writing to President Droupadi Murmu on November 27, 2026, and calling for greater representation of marginalised communities in the higher judiciary.

stories.title: Can India’s Capital Markets Unlock The Viksit Bharat Dream? ICRA-ASSOCHAM Outlines Roadmap For Financial Growth
stories.summary: India’s capital markets are expected to play a pivotal role in financing the country’s transition towards a developed economy by 2047, with greater market depth, liquidity and institutional participation emerging as critical priorities, according to an ICRA-ASSOCHAM report released on Friday. The report highlighted the need for a more inclusive financial ecosystem capable of mobilising long-term investments and supporting sustainable economic growth .

stories.title: Rs 11-Lakh Chandelier, Rs 6-Lakh Temple: Inside Kejriwal’s Former ‘Sheesh Mahal’, Soon To Open To Public
stories.summary: After remaining the BJP's key criticism of the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and its common man-friendly image, former Delhi chief minister Arvind Kejriwal's erstwhile official residence was opened for a media tour on Friday. Dubbed the 'Sheesh Mahal', the Kejriwal's former Flagstaff Road bungalow was used as ammunition by the BJP ahead of the Delhi Assembly election last year.

stories.title: Special Trains Being Run For Devotees Willing to Attend Kali Puja in Dakshin Dinajpur (West Bengal)
stories.summary: To facilitate ease of travel for devotees attending Bolla Kali Puja in Dakshin Dinajpur district of West Bengal, Northeast Frontier Railway (NFR) will operate passenger special trains between New Coochbehar and Balurghat from 27th to 29th November 2026. NFR has also arranged two-minute stoppages at Eklakhi station under Katihar Division for four pairs of special trains on select journeys, giving devotees additional travel options during the puja.

stories.title: Aarti's defamation case against Kenisha: HC orders Dec 3 appearance
stories.summary: Ravi Mohan and Aarti are currently facing a series of legal battles amid their separation and pending divorce. Aarti's recent action involves a defamation case against singer Kenisha Francis, which is set for court hearing. Additionally, Aarti has requested that Ravi's visitation rights to their two sons be revoked, citing concerns over his behavior and unpaid maintenance fees.

stories.title: 'Deepam to be lit tomorrow': Furious SC suspends temple trust, asks CRPF to step in
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has mandated that a Karthigai Deepam lamp be lit atop Deepathoon, following the suspension of the temple's board of trustees and the appointment of receivers for management. Security responsibilities have been given to the CRPF for the temple and nearby hill. Moreover, the court issued contempt notices to several Tamil Nadu officials for non-compliance and cautioned against any actions that might threaten constitutional order.

stories.title: Viral VIDEO: Passenger Blows Conch, Lights Diya Inside AC Train Coach To Perform Pooja; Railways Seeks Details For Probe
stories.summary: A video showing a passenger performing puja inside an air-conditioned train coach has gone viral on social media, triggering concerns over passenger safety and the misuse of public transport spaces. The clip reportedly shows the passenger conducting religious rituals, lighting a diya (oil lamp) and blowing a conch inside the moving train.
